# ui::PathGeometry

Header: `winui/render/PathGeometry.hpp`.

A set of figures and the fill rule between them: what a [Path](../controls/shapes.md#uipath), a path icon or any other [Shape](../controls/shapes.md#uishape) draws.

A default-constructed PathGeometry is empty and draws nothing. Build one with the static builders or parse path markup, then hand it to a [ui::PathControl](../controls/shapes.md#class-pathcontrol), to [`ui::Path{.data = ...}`](../controls/shapes.md#uipath), to [IconSource::path()](icon-source.md#path), or straight to [Renderer::draw_geometry()](renderer.md#draw_geometry).

Example: 
```cpp
const auto arrow = ui::PathGeometry::parse("F1 M 20,20L 24,10L 24,24L 5,24"); // nullopt if malformed
const ui::PathGeometry pill   = ui::PathGeometry::rectangle(ui::Rect{0, 0, 40, 16}, 8.0f, 8.0f);
const ui::PathGeometry both[] = {*arrow, pill};
const ui::PathGeometry group  = ui::PathGeometry::group(both, ui::FillRule::Nonzero);

window.set_content(ui::Path{
    .data   = group,
    .fill   = ui::colors::Black,
    .stroke = ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 120, 215),
});
```

## figures

```cpp
std::vector<PathFigure> figures
```

The figures, drawn in order; all share [`fill_rule`](#fill_rule).

## fill_rule

```cpp
FillRule fill_rule = FillRule::EvenOdd
```

How overlapping figures decide what is inside (markup `F0`/`F1`).

## line

```cpp
static PathGeometry line(Point from, Point to)
```

A line: one open figure from `from` to `to`.

## rectangle

```cpp
static PathGeometry rectangle(const Rect& rect, float radius_x = 0.0f, float radius_y = 0.0f)
```

A rectangle, also a [Rectangle](../controls/shapes.md#uirectangle) shape's outline: a closed figure, its corners rounded by elliptical arcs of `radius_x` by `radius_y` when either is positive (each clamped to half the rect), sixteen points in all.

## ellipse

```cpp
static PathGeometry ellipse(Point center, float radius_x, float radius_y)
```

An ellipse: a closed figure of four quarter arcs.

## polyline

```cpp
static PathGeometry polyline(std::span<const Point> points, bool closed, FillRule rule = FillRule::EvenOdd)
```

A [Polyline](../controls/shapes.md#uipolyline) (`closed` false) or [Polygon](../controls/shapes.md#uipolygon) (`closed` true): straight segments through `points`. Fewer than two points is empty.

## group

```cpp
static PathGeometry group(std::span<const PathGeometry> members, FillRule rule = FillRule::EvenOdd)
```

A group: every member's figures under one fill rule.

## parse

```cpp
static std::optional<PathGeometry> parse(std::string_view markup)
```

Parses path markup such as `F1 M 0,10 L 5,0 L 10,10 Z`. Returns nullopt when the markup doesn't parse. An empty string is an empty geometry.

## empty

```cpp
bool empty() const
```

True when there are no figures (the geometry draws nothing).

## bounds

```cpp
Rect bounds() const
```

The tight bounding box of every figure (Bézier extrema, not control points). An empty geometry has an empty rect at the origin.

## transformed

```cpp
PathGeometry transformed(const Matrix& m) const
```

Every point run through `m`. Béziers stay Béziers: an affine transform of the control points is the transform of the curve.

## fill_contains

```cpp
bool fill_contains(Point p) const
```

Whether `p` is inside the filled area under the fill rule, with curves flattened finely enough for hit testing.
